title: See Justin Timberlake Make Surprise Appearance at Don Toliver’s Miami Concert
summary: Taking the stage for first time in over a year, singer joins rapper for "Rock Your Body" and "Body"
whatHappening: Justin Timberlake made a surprise stage appearance at Don Toliver's Miami concert, marking his first performance in over a year. The pop icon joined the rapper to perform "Rock Your Body" and "Body."
whoInvolved: Justin Timberlake is a Grammy Award-winning singer, songwriter, and dancer dubbed the "Prince of Pop" and recognized as one of the greatest pop stars of the 21st century. Don Toliver is a Houston-based rapper and songwriter signed to Travis Scott's Cactus Jack Records who has collaborated with major hip-hop figures.
whyMatters: The appearance signals Timberlake's return to live performance after an extended absence, potentially indicating renewed touring activity from one of pop music's biggest names. The cross-genre collaboration between Timberlake and Toliver also highlights the ongoing intersection of pop and hip-hop at major concert events.
articleBody:
Justin Timberlake made a surprise appearance at Don Toliver's Miami concert, stepping on stage for the first time in over a year to perform alongside the Houston rapper. According to Rolling Stone, Timberlake joined Toliver to perform the hit "Rock Your Body" along with "Body," delighting attendees with an unexpected moment.

The performance marks a significant moment for Timberlake, who has maintained a relatively low public profile in recent months. The pop superstar, who has earned ten Grammy Awards, four Primetime Emmy Awards, three Brit Awards, and nine Billboard Music Awards throughout his career, is widely recognized as one of the best-selling music artists of all time. Billboard previously named him one of the Greatest Pop Stars of the 21st Century, cementing his status as a transformative figure in modern pop music.

Don Toliver has emerged as a rising force in hip-hop following his 2018 debut mixtape Donny Womack and subsequent collaborations with major artists. Signed to Travis Scott's Cactus Jack Records in a joint venture with Atlantic Records, Toliver has built a presence that bridges rap and melodic styles, making the collaboration with Timberlake a natural pairing of complementary musical approaches.

The Miami performance itself represents a notable moment for concert culture, where surprise guest appearances continue to generate significant fan engagement and social media buzz. For Timberlake, the appearance suggests renewed momentum after his extended time away from live performance, while for Toliver it represents the kind of high-profile collaboration that elevates a younger artist's profile within the industry.

Fans and industry observers will likely watch for further announcements about Timberlake's touring plans, given the significance of this return to the stage. The collaboration also underscores the contemporary music landscape, where pop and hip-hop artists frequently share stages and audiences.

title: See King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard Bring Out Max Weinberg at Queens Show
summary: E Street Band drummer fills in for his son and friend of the band Jay Weinberg at Australian psych-rockers' Forest Hills Stadium concert
whatHappening: Max Weinberg, the legendary E Street Band drummer, took the stage at King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's Forest Hills Stadium concert in Queens, stepping in as a special guest. The iconic drummer filled in for Jay Weinberg, his son and a friend of the Australian psych-rock band.
whoInvolved: Max Weinberg is an American drummer best known as Bruce Springsteen's longtime E Street Band drummer and as bandleader for Conan O'Brien's late-night television shows. King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard is an Australian rock band formed in Melbourne in 2010, known for their energetic live performances and prolific output across multiple genres.
whyMatters: The appearance represents a rare cross-generational and cross-genre collaboration, bringing together a classic rock legend with a contemporary psych-rock act. It highlights the continuing reach and influence of established musicians while underscoring the collaborative spirit within modern rock communities.
articleBody:
Max Weinberg, the drummer synonymous with Bruce Springsteen's E Street Band for decades, made a surprise appearance at King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's Queens show, bringing his formidable presence to the Australian psych-rockers' Forest Hills Stadium concert. According to Rolling Stone, Weinberg filled in for Jay Weinberg, his son and a friend of the band, in a moment that bridged classic and contemporary rock worlds.

King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, formed in Melbourne in 2010, has built a reputation as one of rock's most dynamic live acts, known for staging energetic performances and exploring a wide range of genres across their prolific catalog. The band's current lineup includes Stu Mackenzie, Ambrose Kenny-Smith, Cook Craig, Joey Walker, Lucas Harwood, and Michael Cavanagh. Their willingness to invite special guests to their performances reflects the collaborative ethos that has defined their approach to live music.

Max Weinberg's appearance carried particular significance given his decades-long tenure as the heartbeat of the E Street Band. Beyond his work with Springsteen, Weinberg has maintained a high profile as a television personality, serving as bandleader for Conan O'Brien on both Late Night and The Tonight Show. His participation in the Forest Hills show demonstrated the kind of spontaneous collaboration that energizes live rock performances and creates memorable moments for audiences.

Jay Weinberg, Max's son, has established his own drumming credentials, having worked with both Slipknot and Suicidal Tendencies. His friendship with King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, strong enough to make him a regular part of their live performances, created the circumstances for Max's guest appearance. The intergenerational dynamic—with the elder Weinberg stepping in for his son—added an extra layer of meaning to an already notable moment.

The Queens concert showcased the kind of cross-genre pollination that continues to define rock music in the contemporary landscape, where established legends and emerging acts frequently find common ground on stage. For audiences at Forest Hills Stadium, the evening provided an unexpected encounter with one of rock's most accomplished and enduring drummers.

articleBody:

title: Janie Bradford, Motown Songwriter Who Co-Wrote ‘Money (That’s What I Want’), Dead at 87
summary: "Janie was there with me from the very beginning, before there was even a Motown," Berry Gordy writes in tribute to label's receptionist-turned-hit songwriter
whatHappening: Janie Bradford, the pioneering Motown songwriter and receptionist who co-wrote the enduring hit 'Money (That's What I Want)', has died at 87. Berry Gordy, Motown's founder, paid tribute to her as a foundational figure in the label's early history.
whoInvolved: Janie Bradford was an American songwriter who rose from receptionist to hit-maker at Motown Records, the Detroit-based label founded by Berry Gordy Jr. in 1959. Bradford's most famous collaboration with Gordy, 'Money', became a standard recorded by artists including Barrett Strong, The Beatles, and The Rolling Stones.
whyMatters: Bradford's death marks the passing of a key architect of Motown's sound during its formative years, when the label was establishing itself as a powerhouse of American popular music. Her songwriting legacy, particularly 'Money', has endured across generations and genres, influencing rock, pop, and soul music for over six decades.
articleBody:
Janie Bradford, a songwriter who helped shape Motown Records' golden era and co-wrote one of popular music's most recorded songs, has died at 87. Berry Gordy, the legendary founder of Motown, paid homage to Bradford's irreplaceable role in the label's creation, writing that "Janie was there with me from the very beginning, before there was even a Motown."

Bradford began her career at Motown as a receptionist, a position that placed her at the heart of the nascent label during its earliest days. Founded by Gordy as Tamla Records on January 12, 1959, and incorporated as Motown Record Corporation on April 14, 1960, the Detroit-based operation was still finding its footing when Bradford joined. Her ascent from front-desk duties to songwriter reflects both her talent and the fluid, entrepreneurial environment Gordy cultivated at the label whose name became synonymous with Detroit itself.

Bradford's most enduring contribution to music came through her collaboration with Gordy on "Money (That's What I Want)." Originally recorded by Barrett Strong, the song became a template for what Motown would become: a bridge between rhythm and blues and mainstream pop. According to Rolling Stone, the track's infectious groove and straightforward lyrical hook made it irresistible to artists across genres. The song entered the rock canon when The Beatles recorded it for their second album, "With The Beatles," and it also appeared on The Rolling Stones' first UK EP, cementing its status as a standard.

What made "Money" remarkable was its staying power. Decades after its initial release, the song continued to be recorded and reimagined by successive generations of musicians, a testament to both Bradford and Gordy's songwriting acumen. The track transcended the soul and R&B markets where it originated, becoming a touchstone in rock and pop music—a rare achievement that underscored Bradford's gift for crafting hooks and narratives that resonated across audiences.

Bradford's career at Motown reflected a broader pattern within the label: talented individuals found opportunities to grow and contribute across multiple roles. While she may not have achieved the household-name status of some Motown artists, her influence rippled through the label's output and, by extension, through popular music itself. Her presence during Motown's formative period made her a custodian of the label's creative spirit during the years when it was establishing the sound that would define a generation.

With Bradford's passing, the music world loses one of the few remaining figures who witnessed and shaped Motown's transformation from a local Detroit operation into a global force in popular music.

title: Olivia Rodrigo Releases New Song ‘Serena Joy’ Via CD Single at One Indie Record Shop
summary: Tustin, California’s Analog Music Shop, the record store closest to singer's Daisy Chain Fields, was recipient of Handmaid's Tale-inspired track ahead of its digital release; all 500 copies have sold out
whatHappening: Olivia Rodrigo has released a new song called 'Serena Joy' as a CD single exclusively at Analog Music Shop in Tustin, California, ahead of its digital release. All 500 physical copies have already sold out.
whoInvolved: Olivia Rodrigo is an American singer-songwriter and actress who rose to prominence through her roles in the Disney Channel series Bizaardvark and the Disney+ series High School Musical: The Musical: The Series. Analog Music Shop is an independent record store in Tustin, California, located near Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields.
whyMatters: The exclusive physical release strategy highlights how artists are leveraging independent record retailers to build buzz and create scarcity around new music. The rapid sellout of all 500 copies demonstrates ongoing consumer demand for physical music formats and the power of limited-edition releases to drive immediate commercial interest.
articleBody:
Singer-songwriter Olivia Rodrigo has released a new song titled 'Serena Joy' as a CD single at Analog Music Shop in Tustin, California, marking an unconventional rollout strategy that prioritizes independent retail before the track becomes available digitally. According to Rolling Stone, all 500 physical copies of the single have sold out, underscoring strong demand from fans willing to visit a brick-and-mortar location for exclusive access to new material.

The track takes its title from The Handmaid's Tale, the 1985 dystopian novel by Margaret Atwood set in the totalitarian Republic of Gilead. Serena Joy is a significant character within that narrative universe, suggesting Rodrigo may be drawing thematic inspiration from Atwood's exploration of power, control, and resistance in a patriarchal society. By naming the song after this character, Rodrigo appears to be engaging with the novel's complex political commentary.

Anolog Music Shop's selection as the exclusive first retail outlet is particularly notable given its proximity to Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields. The decision to route a new release through a single independent record store represents a deliberate choice to support local retail and create a geographically specific fan event rather than pursuing a conventional simultaneous multi-platform release.

Rodrigo's career trajectory has encompassed both music and acting. She gained initial recognition through television work, appearing in commercials and the 2015 direct-to-video film An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success before landing her breakthrough roles in Bizaardvark and High School Musical: The Musical: The Series. Her transition to recording artist has proven commercially successful, making her subsequent releases closely watched by both fans and industry observers.

The rapid sellout of the physical CD single illustrates ongoing consumer appetite for limited-edition music releases and tangible formats at a time when streaming dominates industry consumption patterns. The exclusive retail strategy also reflects how artists can use scarcity and geographic specificity to generate organic interest and reward dedicated local fan bases, a model that may prove influential for future independent releases.

title: Buckcherry Members ‘Unharmed’ After Tour Bus Involved in Tragic ‘Multi-Vehicle Accident’
summary: "Authorities have confirmed that the collision that occurred ahead of our bus resulted in a fatality," said the band in a statement
whatHappening: Hard rock band Buckcherry's tour bus was involved in a multi-vehicle accident on the road. While the band members escaped unharmed, the collision resulted in at least one fatality among other vehicles involved.
whoInvolved: Buckcherry is an American hard rock band from Anaheim, California, formed in 1995 and reformed in 2005 by lead vocalist Josh Todd and lead guitarist Keith Nelson. The band is known for their 2006 crossover hit "Crazy Bitch" and continues to tour.
whyMatters: The incident highlights the dangers inherent in touring life for musicians and raises awareness about highway safety involving large vehicles. While the band escaped injury, the fatality among other motorists underscores the serious consequences of multi-vehicle collisions.
articleBody:
Buckcherry's tour bus was involved in a multi-vehicle accident that resulted in a fatality, though all band members aboard escaped without injury. In a statement, the band confirmed the severity of the incident, noting that "authorities have confirmed that the collision that occurred ahead of our bus resulted in a fatality," according to Rolling Stone. The exact circumstances of how the accident unfolded and which vehicles were involved in the broader collision remain under investigation by authorities.

Buckcherry, the American hard rock outfit from Anaheim, California, has maintained an active touring schedule since their 2005 reformation. Originally formed in 1995, the band dissolved in 2002 after releasing two albums—their self-titled debut in 1999 and Time Bomb in 2001. Lead vocalist Josh Todd and lead guitarist Keith Nelson revived the band in 2005 and released a new album in 2006 titled 15, which featured their biggest crossover success, "Crazy Bitch," and marked a significant moment in their career resurgence.

Tour bus accidents, while relatively uncommon given the volume of touring that occurs across the music industry, carry particular gravity due to the number of people typically aboard and the scale of the vehicles involved. The fact that Buckcherry's entire touring party remained unharmed in this incident is fortunate, though it provides little comfort to those affected by the fatal collision.

The band has not released additional details about the accident or whether their tour schedule will be affected. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the multi-vehicle collision, which will likely determine the cause and responsibility for the fatal outcome.

articleBody:

title: Tupac Jurors See Keffe D’s First Public Interview About Killing: ‘I Got Cancer…Nothing Else to Lose’
summary: The jury also heard Keffe claim in a 2009 police interview that alleged gunman Orlando Anderson “peed on his hands” after the shooting to wash away gunpowder
whatHappening: Jurors in the Tupac Shakur murder trial are hearing testimony from Keffe D, a key witness who has now given his first public interview detailing his account of the 1996 killing. In a 2009 police interview played for the court, Keffe D claims that alleged gunman Orlando Anderson used an unusual method to dispose of evidence after the shooting.
whoInvolved: Keffe D is a witness in the case involving the murder of Tupac Shakur, the influential rapper and activist who was shot in a drive-by shooting on September 7, 1996, in Las Vegas. Orlando Anderson is identified as the alleged gunman in the case that has remained unsolved for nearly three decades.
whyMatters: This testimony represents a major development in one of hip-hop's most infamous unsolved murders, offering potential breakthrough evidence after 28 years. The trial outcome could finally provide closure to Tupac's family and fans while setting a significant precedent for cold-case prosecution in high-profile crimes.
articleBody:
Jurors in the long-awaited trial over Tupac Shakur's 1996 murder are now seeing evidence from Keffe D, a witness whose testimony may finally shed light on one of the music industry's most enduring mysteries. According to Rolling Stone, the jury heard a 2009 police interview in which Keffe D claims that alleged gunman Orlando Anderson engaged in an unusual attempt to cover his tracks immediately after the shooting—specifically, that Anderson "peed on his hands" to wash away gunpowder residue.

On September 7, 1996, at 11:15 p.m., Tupac Shakur, then 25 years old, was struck by four rounds from a .40-caliber Glock 22 pistol in a drive-by shooting at a Las Vegas intersection. The shots hit Shakur twice in the chest, once in the arm, and once in the thigh. Suge Knight, the driver of Shakur's vehicle, was grazed by a bullet during the attack. Shakur died six days later from his injuries, and the case went cold for nearly three decades.

Keffe D's willingness to testify publicly now appears tied to his health. In the interview, he reportedly stated "I got cancer… nothing else to lose," suggesting that his terminal diagnosis has motivated him to finally speak openly about the circumstances of the shooting. This kind of deathbed confession or late-life testimony has occasionally broken open cold cases where witnesses previously feared retaliation or other consequences.

The specificity of Keffe D's account—including the detail about Anderson's method of attempting to remove gunpowder evidence—provides investigators with forensic and behavioral details that could corroborate or contradict other evidence presented in the trial. Such granular testimony is often crucial in cases where decades have passed and physical evidence may have degraded or been lost.

Tupac Shakur was one of the most influential musical artists of the 20th century, a rapper and actor whose work addressed social injustice and the marginalization of African Americans, though he was also closely associated with gangsta rap. His death at 25 cut short the career of an artist who had already sold millions of records and established himself as both a cultural and political voice. The unsolved nature of his murder has cast a long shadow over hip-hop history, making this trial a potential turning point in a case that has remained open longer than most homicides.

title: Bonnaroo Taking ‘Much-Needed Year Off’ in 2027
summary: Sorry Bonnaroovians: The beloved Manchester, Tennessee, festival won't be held next summer
whatHappening: Bonnaroo, the four-day music festival held annually in Manchester, Tennessee, will not take place in 2027. The festival is taking what organizers are calling a "much-needed year off" to regroup.
whoInvolved: Bonnaroo is developed and operated by Superfly Presents and AC Entertainment, the companies behind the longtime festival that has drawn music fans to Tennessee each summer. The festival has been a fixture on the American music festival calendar since its inception.
whyMatters: The hiatus signals potential strain on even established festival operations, whether from financial pressures, logistical challenges, or the need to refresh the event's appeal after years of continuous operation. For fans and the local Manchester economy, the absence will be felt keenly, as Bonnaroo generates significant tourism and cultural attention annually.
articleBody:
Bonnaroo will not happen in 2027. According to Rolling Stone, the beloved Manchester, Tennessee, festival is taking what organizers describe as a "much-needed year off" next summer, marking an unexpected break in the festival's annual schedule.

Bonnaroo is an American annual four-day music festival developed and founded by Superfly Presents and AC Entertainment. Since its inception, the festival has become a major fixture on the summer music circuit, drawing thousands of attendees to the Manchester fairgrounds each year for performances spanning multiple genres and stages.

The decision to pause operations comes at a time when music festivals across the country face mounting operational demands. Running a multi-day event of Bonnaroo's scale requires coordinating logistics, securing artist lineups, managing infrastructure, and handling the complex permitting and safety requirements that come with hosting tens of thousands of attendees.

While organizers have not detailed specific reasons for the hiatus, the timing suggests a need to reassess and rebuild after years of consecutive annual events. Taking a year off allows festivals to evaluate their current operations, explore new creative directions, and address any underlying challenges—whether financial, operational, or strategic—without the pressure of an immediate deadline.

For Bonnaroo fans, the news is disappointing. The festival has cultivated a devoted following over its history, and the Manchester event has become a summer tradition for many music lovers. The local Manchester economy also benefits from the festival's annual influx of visitors and associated spending.

Organizers have not announced a specific timeline for Bonnaroo's return, though the phrasing of a "much-needed year off" suggests the intention is not permanent. Festival enthusiasts will be watching for news about whether the event returns in 2028 and what changes or innovations might accompany its return.

articleBody:

title: Tupac Murder Trial: Jurors Hear ‘Secret’ Police Interview with Keffe D Admitting Role in Shooting
summary: Duane “Keffe D” Davis now says he lied to investigators during the meeting to gain leverage while facing a potential life sentence on drug charges
whatHappening: Jurors in the Tupac Shakur murder trial are hearing testimony from a secret police interview in which Duane "Keffe D" Davis admitted to a role in the 1994 shooting. Davis now claims he lied during that interview to gain leverage while facing potential life imprisonment on drug charges.
whoInvolved: Duane Davis, also known as Keffe D, is a figure connected to the decades-old murder of Tupac Shakur, one of the most influential rappers and cultural activists of the 20th century who sold over 75 million records worldwide. The case involves law enforcement investigators seeking to finally resolve one of hip-hop's most infamous unsolved murders.
whyMatters: The trial represents a rare moment of potential closure in a case that has captivated the public for nearly three decades. The credibility of Davis's statements—whether his admission or his current denial—will be central to whether the murder can finally be prosecuted, making the jury's assessment of his truthfulness potentially decisive in achieving justice for Shakur's death.
articleBody:
Jurors in the murder trial related to Tupac Shakur's death are being presented with a recorded police interview in which Duane "Keffe D" Davis detailed his involvement in the 1994 shooting that killed the legendary rapper. According to Rolling Stone, Davis now claims he intentionally lied to investigators during that encounter, asserting that he provided the false admission to gain leverage in his own legal situation as he faced the prospect of a life sentence on drug charges.

Tupac Amaru Shakur, known by his stage names 2Pac and Makaveli, was an American rapper and actor who became one of the most influential musical artists of the 20th century. His murder on the Las Vegas Strip in September 1994 remained officially unsolved for nearly three decades, making it one of hip-hop's most persistent mysteries. Shakur's body of work addressed social injustice and political issues affecting African Americans, and he sold more than 75 million records worldwide, cementing his status as a cultural icon far beyond music.

The introduction of the secret interview recording into trial proceedings presents a complex evidentiary puzzle for jurors. On one hand, Davis appears on the recording admitting to a role in the shooting—a confession that could be viewed as highly incriminating. On the other hand, his current claim that he fabricated the admission to manipulate investigators creates reasonable doubt about whether any statements he made during that interview can be trusted. This contradiction places the jury in the position of determining not only what happened nearly thirty years ago, but also assessing the credibility and motivation of a key witness whose own account of his actions has fundamentally shifted.

Davis's assertion that he lied to gain leverage reflects a common defense strategy in criminal cases, where defendants or witnesses claim they made false statements under pressure or to achieve some tactical advantage. The drug charges Davis faced at the time of the interview add context to his potential motivation—with his freedom and future at stake, a calculated admission might have seemed a worthwhile trade-off. However, the very fact that he had motive to lie then raises questions about his current testimony and motivations as well.

The trial marks a significant moment in the long-stalled investigation into Shakur's death. For decades, the case languished as a cold file, with no arrests or convictions despite numerous theories and suspects. The decision to finally prosecute, based substantially on Davis's involvement and testimony, suggests that authorities believed they had finally gathered sufficient evidence to move forward. Whether the jury will accept Davis's current version of events or weigh his recorded admission as more credible remains to be seen.

title: Jade Is Her Own Biggest Fan and Has the Spotify Library to Prove It
summary: The pop singer and songwriter joins Rolling Stone's Song Shuffle series, revealing an eclectic mix of songs from Little Mix and her own debut solo album That's Showbiz Baby!
whatHappening: Jade Thirlwall is opening up her music taste in Rolling Stone's Song Shuffle series, sharing an eclectic playlist that spans hits from her former group Little Mix and tracks from her debut solo album That's Showbiz Baby!
whoInvolved: Jade Thirlwall is an English singer who rose to prominence as a member of Little Mix, the first group to win the UK X Factor in its eighth series. The girl group released six studio albums and achieved nineteen UK top-ten singles before going into hiatus in 2022, with Thirlwall now pursuing a solo career.
whyMatters: The interview offers insight into Thirlwall's artistic evolution as she transitions from group member to solo artist, revealing how both her past and present work shape her musical identity. Her participation in the series highlights the continued cultural relevance of both Little Mix's legacy and emerging solo ventures from the group's members.
articleBody:
Jade Thirlwall is taking fans behind the curtain of her musical tastes, and the results show a self-aware artist who isn't shy about celebrating her own work. The English singer and songwriter has joined Rolling Stone's Song Shuffle series, a recurring feature that invites musicians to reveal their personal playlists and discuss the songs that matter most to them.

Thirlwall's selections paint a portrait of an artist comfortable with her past while forging ahead creatively. The playlist weaves together material from Little Mix, the girl group that propelled her to international stardom, alongside songs from That's Showbiz Baby!, her debut solo album. This mix reflects both where she's been and where she's heading—a natural progression for an artist navigating life after a major chapter of her career.

Thirlwall's journey to this point has been unconventional. She began pursuing music professionally at age 15, auditioning for The X Factor three times before finally making an impact on the show's eighth series. Little Mix formed during that competition and became the first group to win the UK's original X Factor, going on to become the show's most successful winning act. Over more than a decade together, the group released six studio albums and accumulated nineteen UK top-ten singles, five of which reached number one, establishing themselves as a defining act of their generation.

According to Rolling Stone, Thirlwall's participation in Song Shuffle underscores how artists reflect their own work and influences in their listening habits. The eclectic nature of her playlist suggests someone who draws inspiration widely, even as she continues developing her solo identity following Little Mix's hiatus in 2022.

For fans of both Little Mix and Thirlwall's emerging solo career, the playlist offers a window into how she views her catalog and what drives her artistically. It's a reminder that even artists at the center of global pop phenomena maintain their own fandom and creative reference points—and aren't afraid to show it.

articleBody:

articleBody:

Heavy Is the Crown marks a significant collaborative effort for both artists, combining .Paak's established production sensibility and vocal range with Cordae's contemporary rap style. The upcoming album is expected to showcase both artists' strengths while creating something distinct from their individual work.

title: Alex Lifeson Quit Weed for Rush’s Tour. These 10 Musicians Gave It Up, Too (Or At Least Tried)
summary: We look at other musicians — from Miley Cyrus to Willie Nelson to Paul McCartney to SZA — who've talked about quitting
whatHappening: Alex Lifeson, guitarist for the Canadian rock band Rush, quit cannabis use ahead of the band's tour. Rolling Stone has compiled a list of ten other musicians—including Miley Cyrus, Willie Nelson, Paul McCartney, and SZA—who have similarly quit or attempted to quit using marijuana.
whoInvolved: Alex Lifeson is the guitarist and co-founder of Rush, the legendary Canadian rock band formed in Toronto in 1968. Rush maintained its classic three-member lineup of Lifeson, Geddy Lee, and Neil Peart from 1974 until the band's initial dissolution in 2015, eventually reforming in 2025.
whyMatters: Lifeson's decision highlights how even veteran musicians at the peak of their careers reassess their personal habits in preparation for major performances. The broader list of musicians who have quit or reduced cannabis use reveals shifting attitudes toward substance use within the music industry, driven by health concerns, creative clarity, and professional demands.
articleBody:
Alex Lifeson has made the decision to quit marijuana as Rush prepares for its upcoming tour, joining a notable group of musicians who have taken similar steps. The guitarist and co-founder of Rush, one of rock's most enduring acts, is prioritizing sobriety ahead of what will be a significant moment for the band that has commanded devoted audiences since its formation in Toronto in 1968.

Lifeson's choice is far from unique in the music world. According to Rolling Stone, a range of high-profile artists have publicly discussed quitting cannabis or attempting to do so, including Miley Cyrus, Willie Nelson, Paul McCartney, and SZA. The magazine compiled a list of ten musicians with similar stories, underscoring that this decision crosses genre lines and career stages.

Rush itself carries particular weight in rock history. The band's classic lineup—Lifeson on guitar alongside Geddy Lee on bass and vocals and Neil Peart on drums—took shape in 1974 and remained unchanged for more than four decades until the band's initial dissolution in 2015. That stability and longevity made Rush a powerhouse in progressive rock, known for technical virtuosity and elaborate compositions that demanded peak cognitive performance from all members.

For touring musicians, the physical and mental demands are substantial. Extended travel, nightly performances, and the need for precision in complex arrangements all benefit from clarity and focus. Lifeson's decision to eliminate cannabis use before hitting the road reflects a practical reassessment of what his body and mind require to deliver the performances that Rush's audience expects.

The willingness of musicians across different genres and generations to discuss their substance use—whether quitting, reducing, or maintaining—marks a shift in how the industry talks about these issues. Where previous decades saw drug use largely treated as part of rock mythology, contemporary artists are more candid about making deliberate health choices. This transparency may encourage fans and younger musicians to examine their own habits without shame.

As Lifeson and Rush prepare for their tour, the guitarist's decision serves as a reminder that even veteran performers continuously reassess their personal practices in service of their craft.

title: Green Day’s Mike Dirnt to Sell One-of-a-Kind Bass Guitars, Clothing, More on Reverb
summary: Collection includes Dookie, Nimrod, and American Idiot-era bass guitars, alongside other gear and clothing spanning musician's career on Reverb
whatHappening: Mike Dirnt, bassist and co-founder of Green Day, is selling a curated collection of his personal bass guitars, gear, and clothing through Reverb, the online marketplace for musical instruments. The collection spans decades of the band's career, including iconic instruments from the Dookie, Nimrod, and American Idiot eras.
whoInvolved: Mike Dirnt is the co-founder, bassist, and backing vocalist of Green Day, the American rock band formed in 1987 in Rodeo, California. Reverb is a major online platform specializing in buying and selling musical instruments and gear.
whyMatters: This sale offers fans and collectors rare access to instruments central to some of punk rock's most defining albums, while also reflecting a growing trend of legacy artists monetizing memorabilia. For Dirnt personally, the sale represents a curated dispersal of career artifacts that might otherwise remain private or undocumented.
articleBody:
Mike Dirnt, the bassist and co-founder of Green Day, is opening up his personal archive to fans and collectors through a special sale on Reverb, the online marketplace for musical instruments and gear. According to Rolling Stone, the collection includes bass guitars from the band's most celebrated album eras—Dookie, Nimrod, and American Idiot—along with additional equipment and clothing that chronicle Dirnt's decades-long career in one of punk rock's most influential bands.

Green Day formed in Rodeo, California, in 1987, with Dirnt and lead singer Billie Joe Armstrong as founding members; drummer Tré Cool joined in 1990. The band achieved massive commercial success with their 1994 major-label debut Dookie, released through Reprise Records, which became a breakout phenomenon and eventually shipped over 20 million copies in the United States alone. That album, along with subsequent releases like Nimrod and the Grammy-winning American Idiot, helped reignite mainstream interest in punk rock and cemented Green Day's place as one of the defining rock bands of their generation.

The bass guitars being offered on Reverb represent tangible connections to those pivotal moments in rock history. Each instrument carries the sonic and visual history of the records and tours that shaped modern punk, making them particularly valuable to dedicated fans and serious collectors. By choosing Reverb as the sales platform, Dirnt is tapping into a community of musicians and enthusiasts who actively buy, sell, and trade professional-grade equipment and rare instruments.

Beyond the guitars, the sale encompasses a broader range of memorabilia reflecting Dirnt's career trajectory. Clothing and other gear spanning his time with Green Day offer fans additional touchpoints to the musician's professional journey. This approach of offering diverse items rather than a single-item auction allows collectors at different levels of investment to potentially acquire something meaningful.

The sale underscores a shift in how legacy musicians approach their personal archives, moving from private storage to public market accessibility. Rather than keeping career artifacts locked away, Dirnt's decision to make them available on a mainstream platform democratizes access to pieces of music history. For those who grew up listening to Dookie or who discovered Green Day through American Idiot, owning an instrument that helped create those soundtracks represents a direct bridge between listener and artist.

title: Suge Knight Gang Associate Dodges Questions at Tupac Trial: ‘Not Gonna Send Him to Prison’
summary: Former gang member James McDonald testified at the trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis
whatHappening: A former gang member testified at the trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis, the man accused of killing Tupac Shakur in 1994, but refused to answer key questions that could implicate him in the crime. The witness, James McDonald, invoked his right against self-incrimination during cross-examination.
whoInvolved: Duane "Keffe D" Davis is on trial for the 1994 murder of Tupac Amaru Shakur, one of the most influential rappers and cultural figures of the 20th century. James McDonald, a former gang associate connected to Suge Knight's circle, was called to testify but resisted providing incriminating details about the shooting.
whyMatters: This testimony marks a critical moment in the decades-long effort to solve Tupac's murder, one of hip-hop's most infamous unsolved cases. The reluctance of witnesses to fully cooperate underscores the lingering code of silence among gang members and the challenges prosecutors face in securing convictions in cases rooted in street violence from three decades ago.
articleBody:
A former gang member took the stand at the trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis on accusations related to the 1994 murder of Tupac Shakur, but repeatedly refused to answer prosecutors' questions, citing his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination. James McDonald's testimony revealed the persistent obstacles courts face when pursuing convictions in decades-old cases involving street violence and gang networks.

Tupac Shakur, known by his stage names 2Pac and Makaveli, was shot and killed in Las Vegas on September 7, 1994, in what became one of hip-hop's most enduring mysteries. The rapper was among the best-selling music artists of all time, with over 75 million records sold worldwide, and was renowned not only for his musical influence but also for his outspoken activism addressing social injustice and the marginalization of African Americans. His death, along with The Notorious B.I.G.'s murder six months later, defined an era of gang-related violence in the music industry.

According to Rolling Stone, McDonald's refusal to answer questions during the Davis trial reflected a recurring challenge in the case: witnesses connected to the shooting have long remained silent, bound by street codes or fear of retaliation. Davis, who was arrested in 2023 after decades of investigation, has been accused of involvement in Tupac's death. The prosecution's case relies heavily on testimony from individuals with direct knowledge of the crime, making witness cooperation essential to establishing guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

McDonald's cryptic statement—that he would not provide answers that might "send him to prison"—suggests he believes his testimony could expose him to criminal liability. This dynamic illustrates the tension inherent in cases where potential accomplices or associates are called to testify. Without their cooperation, prosecutors struggle to reconstruct the events of that fatal night in Las Vegas.

The trial represents a rare moment of accountability in a murder that has haunted the hip-hop community and American culture for three decades. Yet the willingness of witnesses to invoke their constitutional protections underscores how difficult it remains to pierce the silence surrounding street violence, even when decades have passed and fresh investigative efforts have finally brought charges.

title: Watch ZZ Top Perform ‘Tush’ at Band’s Final Concert With Original Lineup
summary: This July 18, 2021, gig in Louisville, Kentucky, marked the end of one of the single most enduring lineups in rock history
whatHappening: ZZ Top performed 'Tush' at their final concert with the classic original lineup on July 18, 2021, in Louisville, Kentucky. The show marked the end of a five-decade run with the same three musicians who defined the band's sound.
whoInvolved: ZZ Top is an American rock band formed in Houston, Texas in 1969, consisting of vocalist-guitarist Billy Gibbons, drummer Frank Beard, and bassist-vocalist Dusty Hill. The trio became one of rock's most iconic and enduring lineups, known for their signature blues-based sound and distinctive visual style.
whyMatters: The concert represents a historic closing chapter for one of rock music's most stable and recognizable bands. The original lineup's five-decade run together is exceptionally rare in rock history, and this performance marked the definitive end of an era that shaped blues-rock for generations.
articleBody:
ZZ Top took the stage in Louisville, Kentucky on July 18, 2021, to perform what would become their final concert with the band's original and iconic three-member lineup. According to Rolling Stone, the performance of their 1975 hit 'Tush' from the album Fandango! captured a moment that closed one of the most remarkable chapters in rock history.

The band, formed in Houston, Texas in 1969, had maintained an extraordinary consistency that few acts in any genre have achieved. Vocalist-guitarist Billy Gibbons, drummer Frank Beard, and bassist-vocalist Dusty Hill played together for more than fifty years, creating a rhythm section and musical identity that became instantly recognizable to fans worldwide. This stability allowed the band to develop and refine a signature sound rooted in Gibbons' blues-inflected guitar work, anchored by the rock-solid partnership of Beard and Hill.

Beyond their musical output, ZZ Top became famous for their distinctive presentation. Gibbons and Hill cultivated matching appearances featuring sunglasses, hats, and long beards that became as much a part of the band's brand as their music. Combined with their sly and humorous lyrics and a reputation for electrifying live performances, the trio built a cultural footprint that extended far beyond typical rock audiences.

The Louisville show in July 2021 represented a natural culmination of an unprecedented run. Five decades with the same three members is virtually unheard of in rock music, where lineup changes, creative differences, and personal circumstances typically force evolution or dissolution. That ZZ Top maintained its core identity and continued touring and recording throughout this entire period speaks to the chemistry between Gibbons, Beard, and Hill, as well as their shared commitment to the music and their fanbase.

For longtime fans and observers of rock history, the performance carried particular weight as a farewell to a configuration that had defined not just ZZ Top's identity, but also served as a touchstone for rock stability itself. The final notes of 'Tush' in Louisville marked the end of an era that had seemed, against all odds, almost permanent.

title: C+C Music Factory Founder Sues Freedom Williams in $30 Million Trademark Lawsuit
summary: Robert Clivillés claims rapper Williams has been making money off the group's name without permission
whatHappening: Robert Clivillés, co-founder of C+C Music Factory, is suing rapper Freedom Williams for $30 million over trademark rights to the group's name. Clivillés claims Williams has been profiting from the C+C Music Factory brand without authorization.
whoInvolved: Robert Clivillés co-founded C+C Music Factory in 1989 alongside David Cole; the group became a major act in late 1980s and early 1990s dance and hip-hop music. Freedom Williams is the original lead rapper of the group's biggest hits and currently holds the trademark rights to the C+C Music Factory name, which he acquired in 2003.
whyMatters: The lawsuit highlights ongoing disputes over intellectual property and band identity in the music industry, particularly when original members disagree on who controls a group's legacy and commercial rights. The outcome could set precedent for how trademark ownership is determined among founding members of long-defunct musical acts.
articleBody:
Robert Clivillés, the co-founder of the 1990s dance and hip-hop group C+C Music Factory, has filed a $30 million trademark lawsuit against rapper Freedom Williams, alleging that Williams has been using and profiting from the group's name without permission. According to Rolling Stone, Clivillés claims that Williams has made substantial income from touring and other commercial activities under the C+C Music Factory banner.

C+C Music Factory was established in 1989 by Clivillés and David Cole and rose to prominence with a string of hit singles including "Gonna Make You Sweat," "Here We Go," "Things That Make You Go Hmmm...," "Just a Touch of Love," and "Keep It Comin'." Williams, who served as the group's lead rapper on these tracks, became closely associated with the act's commercial success. The band ceased recording following Cole's death in 1996, though the group later reformed in 2010 with Eric Kupper stepping in to replace Cole.

The crux of the dispute centers on trademark ownership. Williams acquired the legal rights to the C+C Music Factory name in 2003 and has continued to tour and perform under that banner. Clivillés's lawsuit contests Williams's exclusive right to use the name, arguing that the original co-founder and his estate should retain ownership or at least control over how the brand is commercialized.

The case underscores longstanding tensions within the music industry over artistic identity and intellectual property when founding members of successful groups pursue divergent paths. While Williams has the registered trademark, Clivillés's legal challenge suggests he believes the co-founder's original creative contribution entitles him to a stake in the group's commercial exploitation. The $30 million figure reflects the perceived value of the C+C Music Factory brand and its enduring appeal to audiences decades after the group's original run.

articleBody:

Through conversations like this, emerging artists use the platform to educate listeners about their own references and to signal their place within broader musical conversations. title: Shakira Pledges $1.25 Million to Rebuild Schools Damaged by Earthquake in Colombia
summary: The Colombian singer's Fundación Pies Descalzos will lead an effort to kickstart education in the devastated Chocó region
whatHappening: Shakira is committing $1.25 million to rebuild schools destroyed by an earthquake in Colombia's Chocó region. Her foundation, Fundación Pies Descalzos, will lead the reconstruction and education recovery effort in the affected area.
whoInvolved: Shakira, the Colombian singer and humanitarian, is backing the initiative through Fundación Pies Descalzos (the Barefoot Foundation), a charity she founded in 1997 dedicated to providing quality education to poor and vulnerable Colombian children. The effort targets the Chocó Department, a Pacific region home to the nation's largest Afro-Colombian population.
whyMatters: The pledge addresses critical infrastructure damage to schools in an already vulnerable region, helping restore educational access to displaced and marginalized communities. This intervention is significant both for immediate recovery and for the foundation's long-term mission to ensure every Colombian child can exercise their right to quality education.
articleBody:
Shakira is pledging $1.25 million to rebuild schools devastated by an earthquake in Colombia's Chocó region, marking a major humanitarian response to the natural disaster. The Colombian singer's Fundación Pies Descalzos will lead the effort to restore educational infrastructure and restart programs in the affected area, according to Rolling Stone.

The Barefoot Foundation, established by Shakira in 1997, has long focused on helping poor and impoverished children across Colombia. The organization's stated mission centers on ensuring that every Colombian child can exercise their right to a quality education, with a particular emphasis on serving displaced and vulnerable communities by addressing their unique needs. This latest commitment reflects that core mandate.

Chocó Department, located in Colombia's Pacific region, is home to the largest Afro-Colombian population in the nation, alongside significant populations of Amerindian and mixed African-Amerindian Colombians. The region's geography is distinctive—it is the only Colombian department with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Atlantic Ocean, and it contains all of Colombia's border with Panama. Its capital is Quibdó. The area has historically faced economic challenges and infrastructure gaps, making earthquake recovery particularly difficult for local communities.

The earthquake damage to schools in Chocó represents a severe setback for educational access in a region already struggling with resource constraints. By pledging $1.25 million toward reconstruction, Shakira's foundation aims to accelerate the restoration of learning spaces and enable students to return to classrooms. The commitment underscores the foundation's broader effort to support education in Colombia's most underserved areas.

The rebuilding initiative will not only address physical infrastructure but also help stabilize education systems disrupted by the disaster. For students in Chocó, restoring schools represents a pathway back to normalcy and continuity in their learning. The foundation's targeted approach to vulnerable and displaced communities positions it to understand and meet the specific needs of earthquake-affected families in the region.

title: Tupac Shakur Murder Trial Opens 30 Years After Rapper’s Death: ‘An Act of Revenge’
summary: Jurors will decide whether Duane “Keffe D” Davis played a role in the deadly drive-by shooting that killed Tupac Shakur in September 1996
whatHappening: A murder trial has opened 30 years after the death of rap icon Tupac Shakur, with jurors now tasked with determining whether Duane "Keffe D" Davis played a role in the 1996 drive-by shooting. The case marks a landmark moment in one of hip-hop's most infamous unsolved killings.
whoInvolved: Tupac Shakur was one of the most influential rappers of the 20th century and a prominent political activist, known for addressing social injustice and the marginalization of African Americans through his music while also becoming synonymous with gangsta rap. Duane Davis is the defendant accused in connection with the September 1996 shooting that claimed Shakur's life.
whyMatters: The trial represents a rare moment of potential closure in a case that has haunted the music industry and popular culture for three decades, offering the possibility of finally determining responsibility for one of hip-hop's most transformative artists' death. The outcome could reshape public understanding of the East Coast–West Coast rap feud of the 1990s and set precedent for how cold cases involving gang violence are prosecuted.
articleBody:
Thirty years after Tupac Shakur was shot and killed in a Las Vegas drive-by shooting, a murder trial has finally opened to determine whether Duane "Keffe D" Davis had a role in the rapper's death. The trial represents a watershed moment for a case that has remained unsolved since September 1996, captivating the public imagination and spawning countless theories about who was responsible for killing one of hip-hop's most iconic figures.

Tupac Amaru Shakur, known by his stage names 2Pac and Makaveli, was among the best-selling music artists of all time, with more than 75 million records sold worldwide. Beyond his commercial success, he stood as one of the most influential musical artists of the 20th century and a prominent political activist dedicated to addressing the marginalization of African Americans. His music tackled social injustice and political issues while also becoming intertwined with the emerging gangsta rap genre that dominated the 1990s.

According to Rolling Stone, jurors will now weigh evidence and testimony to determine whether Davis played a part in the drive-by shooting. The prosecution's case appears to center on the theory that the killing was an act of revenge, suggesting motivations rooted in the gang and territorial conflicts that characterized the era. The specifics of Davis's alleged involvement and the exact nature of the revenge motive remain central to the trial's proceedings.

The case arrives at a moment when cold cases involving hip-hop violence are receiving renewed investigative attention. Shakur's death occurred during the height of the East Coast–West Coast rap feud, a cultural and commercial rivalry that defined 1990s hip-hop and contributed to a climate of real-world violence within the industry. His murder, alongside that of fellow rapper The Notorious B.I.G. just six months later, became defining traumas for the genre and remained officially unsolved for three decades.

The trial's opening marks a turning point in the pursuit of accountability for Shakur's death. Whether the jury reaches a conviction or acquittal, the case will finally provide a public accounting of the evidence and arguments surrounding one of popular culture's most enduring mysteries. For hip-hop fans, music historians, and those invested in the Shakur family's search for justice, the trial's outcome carries significance that extends far beyond the courtroom.

title: Taylor Swift Can’t Stop Listening to Phoebe Bridgers’ New Album
summary: The pop superstar celebrated Bridgers' birthday and called Lost Weekend "an absolute triumph" in new social media post
whatHappening: Taylor Swift has publicly praised Phoebe Bridgers' new album Lost Weekend, calling it "an absolute triumph" on social media. Swift shared the compliment while celebrating Bridgers' birthday, highlighting admiration between two of modern music's most acclaimed artists.
whoInvolved: Taylor Swift is one of the world's most influential musicians and the highest-grossing live music artist of all time, known for autobiographical songwriting and frequent artistic reinventions. title: Nashville Star Hayden Panettiere Dies at 36

articleBody:
Hayden Panettiere, the American actress and singer who became a household name through her role as Claire Bennet on the NBC superhero series Heroes, has died at 36. Panettiere's career spanned more than two decades and encompassed leading roles across multiple genres. She starred as Claire Bennet throughout the original run of Heroes from 2006 to 2010, playing a teenage cheerleader grappling with extraordinary abilities in the show's ensemble narrative. Her most recent major television role came in the ABC/CMT musical drama series Nashville, where she played Juliette Barnes from 2012 to 2018. That performance proved particularly acclaimed, earning her two nominations for the Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actress – Series, Miniseries or Television Film and cementing her status as a respected dramatic performer. articleBody:
Cynthia Erivo made a surprise appearance at Ariana Grande's London show at the O2 Arena, where the two Wicked co-stars performed together for fans. Frank Baum's 1900 novel The Wonderful Wizard of Oz and its 1939 film adaptation, reimagining the story from the perspective of the witches at the center of Dorothy Gale's Kansas adventure.

The London performance provides a tantalizing glimpse of the chemistry between the two leads as they prepare to bring their characters' complex relationship to the screen. 'For Good' is one of the musical's most beloved songs, a tender moment that explores the transformative friendship between Elphaba and Glinda. title: Jay Weinberg Reveals He Didn’t Have ‘Legal Ability’ to Work With Other Artists: Part of Him ‘Was Dying’
summary: “Without giving too much attention to any kind of one situation, not having the legal ability to play music with other people was definitely difficult,” drummer says
whatHappening: Jay Weinberg, drummer for Slipknot, has revealed that contractual restrictions prevented him from working with other artists, a limitation he describes as emotionally taxing. The musician is now publicly discussing how the lack of legal freedom to collaborate affected him personally and creatively.
whoInvolved: Jay Weinberg is the drummer for Slipknot, the heavy metal band he joined in 2014 after replacing founding drummer Joey Jordison. whyMatters: Weinberg's comments shed light on the restrictive contractual terms major rock bands impose on members, which can limit artistic growth and personal fulfillment. articleBody:
Jay Weinberg has opened up about the professional constraints that shaped his time as Slipknot's drummer, revealing that contractual limitations prevented him from pursuing collaborative projects outside the band. According to Rolling Stone, the musician explained that "without giving too much attention to any kind of one situation, not having the legal ability to play music with other people was definitely difficult." The restriction, he indicated, took an emotional toll, with part of him feeling like it "was dying" during those periods.

Weinberg joined Slipknot in 2014, taking over the drum chair from founding member Joey Jordison. Before joining the Iowa-based metal act, Weinberg had established himself as a versatile drummer, having played with the punk rock band the Reveling and touring with Bruce Springsteen's E Street Band in 2009 as a substitute for his father, Max Weinberg, who has been Springsteen's drummer for decades. He also had brief stints with Madball and played with Against Me! during 2011 and 2012.

The contractual restrictions Weinberg describes are not uncommon in the music industry, particularly within established bands where members are expected to maintain exclusivity. However, such arrangements can create significant creative frustration for musicians who wish to explore side projects or collaborate with peers. Weinberg's candid remarks suggest that the emotional and artistic cost of such limitations extends beyond simple career management—it affects the psychological well-being of artists bound by them.

By publicly discussing these constraints, Weinberg joins a growing conversation among musicians about the need for greater flexibility in band contracts. His willingness to speak about the experience—and the personal toll it exacted—highlights the tension between an artist's desire for creative exploration and the business interests that drive major touring acts to demand exclusive commitment from their members.

title: Grammys Will Take Asian Music Category Criticism Into Consideration

whatHappening: The Recording Academy is reconsidering its approach to the Best Asian Pop Music Performance Grammy category after facing criticism when BTS decided not to submit their work. whoInvolved: Harvey Mason Jr., CEO of the Recording Academy, which oversees the Grammy Awards—the major U.S. music awards recognizing outstanding achievements across genres. articleBody:
The Grammy Awards' approach to recognizing Asian music is facing fresh scrutiny after BTS opted out of submitting to the Best Asian Pop Music Performance category, prompting the Recording Academy to reconsider its stance. CEO Harvey Mason Jr. initially defended the category when the band's decision became public, but according to Rolling Stone, new conversations with stakeholders may lead the Academy to take the criticism more seriously and explore potential modifications.

BTS, the seven-member South Korean boy band that has dominated global charts since their 2010 formation, wields considerable influence in the music industry. The group consists of Jin, Suga, J-Hope, RM, Jimin, V, and Jung Kook, who co-write or co-produce much of their material. Originally performing as a hip hop group, they have since expanded their musical palette to encompass a wide range of genres, with lyrics addressing themes including mental health, coming-of-age struggles, and self-love. Their decision to bypass the Asian Pop Music category suggests dissatisfaction with how the category is structured or positioned within the broader Grammy framework.

The question of how major awards recognize music from different regions and cultures remains contentious within the industry. Some observers have questioned whether segregating Asian artists into a separate category, rather than allowing them to compete in mainstream pop categories, inadvertently limits their visibility and prestige. Others have raised concerns about the scope of the category itself—whether it adequately represents the diversity of musical styles and national origins across Asia, or whether it creates a catch-all that dilutes meaningful recognition.

Harvey Mason Jr.'s initial defense of the category suggested the Academy viewed it as an inclusive expansion of Grammy recognition. However, his willingness to engage in new conversations with stakeholders signals potential openness to revising that position. The Recording Academy's responsiveness to feedback from major artists like BTS could reshape how future Grammy categories are designed, particularly as the global music industry continues to shift and artists from outside the United States command larger shares of streaming revenue and chart success.

The outcome of these conversations may carry implications beyond the Asian Pop Music category. How the Academy resolves this discussion could influence broader conversations about whether specialized categories genuinely honor artistic achievement or inadvertently create hierarchies within the awards themselves. For BTS and other internationally successful artists, the decision whether to engage with Grammy categories going forward may hinge on whether the Academy demonstrates meaningful change.

title: Frankie Valli Says ‘I Am Not Retired,’ His Brother Bobby Apologizes for Being ‘Misinformed’

whatHappening: Frankie Valli, the 92-year-old Four Seasons frontman, has publicly denied retirement claims on social media after his brother Bobby announced he would be stepping away from performing. Bobby has since apologized for the misinformation.

articleBody:
Frankie Valli has set the record straight about his career status after confusion sparked by his brother's public comments. According to Rolling Stone, Bobby later apologized for being "misinformed" about the situation, effectively retracting his earlier announcement.

The 92-year-old Valli, whose real name is Francesco Stephen Castelluccio, is best known as the lead vocalist of the Four Seasons, the iconic group that defined an era of American popular music. His powerful and unusually distinctive countertenor voice became his signature trademark throughout a career spanning decades. At an age when many performers have long since stepped away from the stage, Valli's clarification suggests he intends to continue working and performing.

The incident underscores the challenges that can arise when family members speak publicly about a performer's plans without clear communication beforehand. Bobby's initial statement, which appeared to announce a major career milestone, was apparently made without confirming the facts with Valli himself. The quick apology and correction prevented prolonged confusion, but the mix-up nonetheless generated enough attention to warrant Valli's direct social media response.

Valli's determination to keep performing reflects a broader pattern among veteran artists who remain active well into their later years. His public refusal to accept the retirement narrative suggests he has no immediate plans to step away from his career, despite his advanced age. The clarification will likely reassure fans and promoters alike regarding his availability for future engagements and appearances.

The incident serves as a reminder of how quickly misinformation can circulate in the age of social media, particularly when it involves public figures. Valli's swift correction and Bobby's apology demonstrate the importance of verification before making major public announcements affecting someone's professional life and public image.
